records.title: West Metro
records.answer: West Metro is an operating two-phase railway extension whose owner now manages long-lived infrastructure, shorter-lived equipment and station access. Its most useful recent result is station-level energy reporting, not a claim that construction completion guarantees every passenger journey.
records.scope: One West Metro project comprising Ruoholahti–Matinkylä and Matinkylä–Kivenlahti. Stations, entrances, depot and associated parking remain components, not extra projects; Espoo and Helsinki remain separate municipalities.
records.stage: Passenger traffic began on the first phase in November 2017 and on the second on December 3, 2022. Later owner reports describe lifecycle maintenance and station-energy work; remaining ancillary works and historical access notices do not establish current equipment availability.

identity_decision.rationale: Count the named West Metro extension once across its two delivery phases. Do not count each station, depot, entrance or parking asset separately, or duplicate Helsinki's existing municipal account. Espoo is a distinct receiving municipality, while the ownership and operating organizations remain institutional context rather than new project identities.

timeline.event: First-phase project plan prepared.
Passenger traffic began on the first phase, as recalled in the owner's lifecycle account.
Espoo council approved the revised second-phase project plan.
Passenger traffic began between Matinkylä and Kivenlahti.
Owner described maintenance arrangements and ancillary works still tied to surrounding development.
Tapiola escalator notice announced staggered summer closures and lift alternatives.
Owner published 2025 station-energy comparisons and described 2026 interventions.

sections.heading: Two phases within one railway
sections.text: West Metro extends the metro westward through two delivery phases: Ruoholahti to Matinkylä, then Matinkylä to Kivenlahti. Its history records planning, excavation, testing and passenger service separately. The first phase began carrying passengers in November 2017; the second opened on December 3, 2022. Those dates describe entry into service, not the completion of every adjacent development. The second-phase account also identifies entrance and parking work outside the initial passenger-opening milestone. Treating each of these components as a new project would inflate the portfolio and obscure the common railway that residents actually use.

sections.heading: Who owns and maintains the system
sections.text: Länsimetro is jointly owned by Espoo and Helsinki and owns and develops the infrastructure. Its governance account separates that role from HSL's timetables and feeder-transport arrangements. The lifecycle account explains that the owner plans and monitors maintenance while Metropolitan Area Transport carries out upkeep across the metro. A maintenance book connects structures and technical systems to detailed plans. Long-term ownership therefore requires coordination beyond the original construction contract. A century-scale infrastructure outlook is not a promise that every component lasts a century: equipment replacement and changing technical requirements belong inside that longer operating life.

sections.heading: Opening and budget have different boundaries
sections.text: Espoo council approved a revised second-phase plan on March 19, 2018. The owner's Swedish account gives a revised budget of €1,159 million and describes changes including larger station areas, the integrated bus terminal and turning facilities. That is a planning envelope, not final audited expenditure. Handover to the operator and the December 2022 passenger opening are later milestones with different tests. The February 2025 lifecycle account still links some entrance and parking work to surrounding construction. Readers should therefore distinguish an operating railway from complete delivery of every associated urban-development element.

sections.heading: Station energy results expose mixed performance
sections.text: The October 2026 owner report compares Keilaniemi's first full monitoring year, 2025, with savings targets after autumn 2024 interventions. Reported heat savings were 258 MWh against a 374 MWh target; electricity savings were 155 MWh against a 102 MWh target. One result fell short while the other exceeded its model. The same report describes ventilation tuning and heat recovery at selected stations. These are station-property results, not train traction or transport-wide emissions. They make a more useful operating account than a single success label, while retaining the operator's reporting basis rather than implying independent verification.

sections.heading: Maintenance must preserve usable routes
sections.text: A July 16 notice on the owner's Tapiola page scheduled the short platform escalators to close in turn between July 20 and August 16, 2026. It identified lift access and alternative circulation, while warning that the western lifts could become crowded. The notice shows how maintenance affects the whole route through a station, not just a machine's repair interval. It remains a historical schedule, not confirmation that the work finished or a live November accessibility advisory. A passenger planning a journey needs current routing information; a retrospective reliability assessment needs actual closure and restoration records.

sections.heading: Evidence test for the next operating account
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: follow a named station from an intervention to a comparable operating period. Pair energy baselines and weather assumptions with maintenance records, replacement costs and passenger-route availability, so a saving is not credited to a service reduction. For accessibility, retain actual outage start and restoration times, the alternatives offered and the capacity of those alternatives. For remaining construction, distinguish acceptance of the entrance or parking asset from occupation of nearby buildings. These separate tests would connect asset stewardship to passenger experience without converting a railway opening into an unsupported claim of continuous performance.

next_artifacts: Named-station energy results with comparable baseline and weather/usage treatment.
Actual Tapiola outage and restoration records, including lift-route availability.
Dated acceptance records for remaining Kivenlahti entrance and associated parking works.

records.title: Espoo
records.answer: Espoo connects metro access, a changing heat system, regional wastewater treatment and household-facing housing and childcare services. Its evidence is strongest when regional totals, company interventions and municipal eligibility rules retain their own boundaries.
records.scope: One Espoo municipality. Shared transport, heating and HSY wastewater systems cross its boundary; company properties and service facilities are examples within the account, not additional places or an expansion of the municipal territory.
records.stage: The city reports a 48% regional-emissions reduction from 1990 to 2025 and the wastewater operator reports 2025 permit compliance. Housing and childcare rules establish service conditions; dated processing notices and planned fixture work do not establish universal delivered access.

identity_decision.rationale: Count Espoo once as a municipality separate from the already counted Helsinki municipality. Explain shared regional services without assigning their full totals to Espoo or counting the HSY catchment as another place. Company buildings, childcare services and individual transport stations illustrate local systems but do not create additional place identities.

timeline.event: Coal-fired district heating ended, according to the city's later emissions account.
Climate Watch updated the housing company's water-saving action record.
HSY published its 2025 wastewater report; the English abstract covers both treatment plants.
The listed childcare fee adjustment took effect.
City published its 2025 regional-emissions comparison with 1990.
City reported delays in processing childcare income statements.

sections.heading: A lower emissions inventory is not every footprint
sections.text: Espoo's August 2026 account reports regional emissions 48% below 1990 levels in 2025, while emissions per resident fell 72%. Those are different comparisons, not interchangeable measures of the same reduction. The city links progress to changes in heating, including the end of coal-fired district heat in April 2024. Transport remained the largest source in the 2025 regional inventory. This inventory does not include the full footprint of goods, food and construction consumed locally but produced elsewhere. It therefore supports a bounded account of territorial progress, not a claim that Espoo has already achieved its broader climate ambitions.

sections.heading: Wastewater crosses the municipal boundary
sections.text: HSY's 2025 report abstract covers Viikinmäki in Helsinki and Blominmäki in Espoo. Together they treated 138.5 million cubic metres, and the operator reports that both met their permit requirements. The combined volume is not Espoo's own wastewater total. Blominmäki completed its third full operating year in 2025 and reported electricity self-sufficiency of 53%; both plants were self-sufficient in heat. These distinctions connect water treatment to energy without treating the two facilities as identical. The abstract is an operator account of annual performance, not an independent inspection of every underlying permit measurement or discharge event.

sections.heading: Housing access is prioritized rather than queued
sections.text: Espoon Asunnot distinguishes state-subsidized rental homes, with income and wealth limits, from privately financed homes without those limits. Its application guidance prioritizes housing need and applicants with lower income and wealth rather than operating a simple chronological queue. Applications remain valid for three months, so keeping one current matters. The guidance also identifies assistance through service points, libraries and housing counselling. These arrangements explain how a resident can enter the selection process, but an eligible application is not an offer or a waiting-time promise. Allocation and occupied-home results require their own dated account.

sections.heading: Childcare entitlement and administration interact
sections.text: The city's fee guidance ties municipal and purchased-service charges to family size, income and hours of care, with an adjustment effective August 1, 2026. Five-year-olds receive four free weekday hours during the specified year; that is not universally free full-day care. A separate August 19 notice reported delays processing income statements and said decisions would be revised after processing. That dated notice does not establish a current November backlog or prove that every correction has been completed. For families, access depends both on the service arrangement and on the administration that turns reported circumstances into a fee decision.

sections.heading: Water savings have a property-level denominator
sections.text: Espoo's Climate Watch describes water-flow measures in 130 Espoon Asunnot properties during 2022–2024 and reports reductions of 16–20% in affected properties. It also records an estimate of 28,800 cubic metres saved in 2025 from the 2024 measures. Those are company intervention claims, not city-wide network-loss figures. The same action record schedules fixture work covering 7,500 apartments during 2026–2028, which must remain planned work. Its February 2026 update date does not date every installation. As the housing stock grows, absolute company consumption and savings in treated properties can move differently without contradiction.

sections.heading: Evidence test for a connected municipal account
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: compare progress at the scale where each service is actually delivered. Keep the municipal emissions inventory separate from household consumption and regional utility totals. For housing and childcare, add allocation, processing and correction times to published eligibility rules, retaining the population and period behind each result. For water-saving fixtures, compare treated properties with their own baselines and record new homes separately. West Metro supplies transport context, but it should not receive causal credit for the city's emissions reduction without an appropriate analysis. This approach makes service trade-offs visible without inventing a synthetic score for Espoo.

next_artifacts: A like-for-like successor regional emissions inventory and separately defined consumption footprint.
Plant-specific wastewater permit results with measured volumes and reporting periods.
Housing allocation and childcare processing/correction results for defined applicant groups.
Completed fixture-work records and comparable property-level water measurements.

records.title: Tampere
records.answer: Tampere's current account combines a future climate and nature budget with completed yard improvements, a regional wastewater plant's first-year report and housing and childcare conditions. Budget approval, construction, service rules and measured outcomes are distinct stages.
records.scope: One Tampere municipality, not the full six-municipality wastewater catchment. Kaupinlaakso, Metsäniitty and Sulkavuori are bounded system examples rather than additional counted project or place identities in this group.
records.stage: Council approved the 2027 budget on November 16, 2026. Dated releases separately describe refurbished yard areas, the wastewater plant's first operating year and a housing proposal at public review; none converts future spending or planned residents into delivered outcomes.

identity_decision.rationale: Count Tampere once within its municipal boundary, preserving the wider wastewater service catchment as regional context. Do not count its district housing proposal, playground or treatment plant as additional projects in this group, and do not extend the place boundary to all neighboring municipalities served by the plant.

timeline.event: City described Kaupinlaakso II's public-review proposal and distinguished the legally valid first plan.
Childcare fee page was updated ahead of the August schedule.
The 2026 childcare fee schedule became effective.
City described Metsäniitty yard improvements and continuing health monitoring.
Sulkavuori operator published a first-year treatment account and acknowledged odour issues.
Council approved the 2027 budget, as reported the following day.
City published the climate and nature budget explanation.

sections.heading: Next year's budget is a commitment to act
sections.text: Tampere council approved the 2027 budget on November 16, 2026. The following day's city account describes climate investments of €13.9 million by the city and €73.1 million by subsidiaries, which are different accounting scopes. Nature measures include tree planting, restoration and preparations for protected areas. These allocations describe authorized future activity, not money already spent or biodiversity already restored. They provide a useful way to follow implementation: the next account should connect the relevant budget line to an actual intervention and outcome. Tampere's climate and nature targets remain targets rather than consequences automatically achieved by the vote.

sections.heading: A greener courtyard is a completed intervention
sections.text: The September Metsäniitty account describes a refurbished daycare and school courtyard with more greenery, shade and natural stormwater management. Children helped choose among proposed improvements, connecting adaptation work to the people using the space. The Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare is monitoring conditions before and after the changes; that research is ongoing, not a completed health-effect result. The city also says the final part of the yard will follow refurbishment of an older building. Completed planting and surface changes can therefore be reported without declaring the entire surrounding project finished or assigning an unmeasured health benefit.

sections.heading: Wastewater results belong to a regional service
sections.text: Sulkavuori's operator reported in September 2026 that the plant had treated 28 million cubic metres during its first operating year. That cumulative figure differs from its stated daily design capacity. The system serves six municipalities: Tampere, Kangasala, Lempäälä, Pirkkala, Vesilahti and Ylöjärvi. Its results cannot be assigned solely to Tampere households. The operator describes strong removal performance but also acknowledges odour incidents and plans broader monitoring in 2027. Quarterly and annual pollutant assessments have different periods; the first-year announcement is not an independent completed calendar-2026 permit audit. Both treatment performance and nuisance management belong in the operating account.

sections.heading: Housing plans depend on transport and services
sections.text: The February 2026 Kaupinlaakso account distinguishes the legally valid first plan, for around 2,500 residents, from a second proposal for around 6,700 at public review. The combined future district is not a population already housed. Development is expected over years and decades around an eastern tram extension, with local education, library and other services concentrated near stops. The proposal also addresses ecological corridors, stormwater and parking. These relationships explain why housing capacity alone is an incomplete delivery measure: transport connections and receiving services have their own construction and opening sequences, which cannot be inferred from a planning illustration.

sections.heading: Childcare fees require the correct version
sections.text: Tampere's childcare page retains both the August 2024 and August 2026 schedules. The newer municipal schedule sets a maximum monthly fee of €335 for one child and bases the assessment on family size, gross income and service need. Mixing its thresholds with the older €311 maximum would misstate the arrangement. The page also distinguishes municipal fees from a service-voucher provider's charge after the municipal voucher. These are service rules, not a calculation for a particular family or evidence that a place is immediately available. The July page-update date and August effective date have different meanings.

sections.heading: Evidence test from allocation to daily service
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: follow one intervention through its own sequence instead of treating the city budget as an outcome score. Match climate spending to completed measures and comparable results; retain the courtyard's monitoring baseline and unfinished area. For wastewater, separate the regional flow denominator, pollutant assessment period and nuisance complaints. For housing, follow actual dwellings, transport openings and receiving-service capacity, not just planned residents. For childcare, track allocation and fee-decision experience alongside dated rules. These connected but independent accounts would show where infrastructure, administration and household experience reinforce one another and where a promised benefit remains undelivered.

next_artifacts: 2027 budget execution linked to completed climate and nature interventions.
Metsäniitty before/after monitoring results and final-area completion record.
Sulkavuori full-period treatment and odour monitoring results for the regional catchment.
Kaupinlaakso II adoption, construction and occupancy artifacts kept separate from tram/service openings.
